title: How to Become a Leader in the Trump Resistance
description:
A 12-Part Online Training Series for Aspiring Organizers and Activists

Overview

In the face of escalating authoritarianism and threats to democratic institutions, the need for effective, principled leadership in the Trump resistance has never been more urgent. This 12-part webinar series is designed to equip participants with the knowledge, skills, and networks necessary to lead nonviolent civil resistance efforts against Donald Trump and his enablers.

What You’ll Learn

Each session offers practical training and strategic insight, covering topics such as:

- Foundations of Nonviolent Resistance: Understanding the principles and history of civil resistance movements.
- Organizing and Mobilization: Building and sustaining grassroots movements.
- Digital Activism: Leveraging online tools for effective advocacy.
- Legal Rights and Protections: Navigating the legal landscape of protest and dissent.
- Media and Messaging: Crafting compelling narratives to galvanize support.

Why Join?

- Expert-Led Sessions: Learn from seasoned organizers and thought leaders in the resistance movement.
- Interactive Learning: Engage in Q&A sessions, workshops, and real-time strategy development.
- Community Building: Connect with like-minded individuals committed to defending democracy.
- Action-Oriented: Translate learning into action with guided assignments and collaborative projects.

Who Should Attend

This series is ideal for:

- New activists seeking foundational knowledge.
- Experienced organizers aiming to refine their strategies.
- Community leaders looking to mobilize local resistance efforts.
- Anyone committed to upholding democratic values and opposing authoritarianism.

Schedule & Registration

- Format: Weekly online sessions via Zoom.
- Duration: 12 weeks.
- Start Date: June 12 at 7p CDT.
- Registration: https://www.mobilize.us/resisttrump/event/795606/

About the Organizers

This series is a collaborative effort by the ResistTrump Campaign, a movement dedicated to lawful, nonviolent civil resistance of Trump and his enablers. Our core values include Collaboration, Integrity, Nonpartisanship, and Professionalism. We are committed to building a future where democracy thrives and authoritarianism is unequivocally rejected.

Oregon’s **Democratic supermajority** was elected to fight for _us_. But right now, crucial programs that keep our communities **housed**, **healthy**, **fed**, and **safe** are on the chopping block—and working families are being left behind.

That’s why we need you on the Capitol steps—_now_.

#### Tell our lawmakers:
We deserve better.
We demand better.
**Fund Oregon Now.**

Bring your voice, your signs, and your people.
This is our moment to **Protect Oregon Now**.

title: NO KINGS Citizens' Parade - Wilmington, Delaware
description:
Hosted by Indivisible Highlands and Beyond; co-hosted with 302 United and Delaware Working Families Power.

Come out for Wilmington’s "No Kings Citizens' Parade" as part of the June 14th National Day of Defiance to counter Trump's ridiculous $45 million birthday parade in DC on this same day. Join us as we parade down Wilmington's own Pennsylvania Avenue to say "NO KINGS!"

June 14th is Flag Day and also the 250th birthday of the army — a day that marks when Americans first organized to stand up to a king. "Trump isn’t honoring that legacy. He’s hijacking it to celebrate himself."

“This country doesn’t belong to a king — and we’re not letting him throw himself a parade funded by tens of millions of our taxpayer dollars while stealing from us and stripping away our rights, our freedoms, and the programs our families rely on. On June 14th, we’re coming together to send one clear message: No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.”

We will gather at the corner of Pennsylvania Avenue and N. Bancroft Parkway in Wilmington. Specifically, we'll meet on grass lawn between the two sides of N. Bancroft Parkway - on the Wawaset Park side of PA Ave., between PA Ave. and W. 11th St. - and march/walk on the sidewalk along Pennsylvania Avenue toward Tower Hill School.

A short rally (with music and guest speakers) will precede the parade. The full roundtrip march is 1.3 miles long.

Bring flags and signs (two-sided, if possible) as well as kazoos, drums, cowbells, etc.

If walking isn't possible for you, please come anyway - with signs and flags - and be part of a Honk and Wave rally along Pennsylvania Ave.

Parking is available on N. Bancroft Parkway and surrounding streets.

Given our commitment to nonviolent action, we expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. If you encounter a heckler or counter-protester (organized or unorganized, from a simple raised finger to a verbal taunt), the rule of thumb is to IGNORE IT!! Do not engage. If necessary, simply turn your back - or walk away.

title: Pride @ Work - Indy Pride Parade
description:
Pride at Work is a nonprofit organization that represents LGBTQ union members and their allies. We are an officially recognized constituency group of the AFL-CIO (American Federation of Labor & Congress of Industrial Organizations) that organizes mutual support between the organized Labor Movement and the LGBTQ Community to further social and economic justice. From our national office in Washington, DC, we coordinate and support more than 20 Chapters across the country.

We seek full equality for LGBTQ Workers in workplaces and unions. We work towards creating a Labor Movement that cherishes diversity, encourages openness, and ensures safety & dignity. We aim to educate the LGBTQ Community about the benefits of a union contract for LGBTQ working people, and to build support and solidarity for the union movement in the LGBTQ community.

We organize in the spirit of the union movement's historic motto, "An Injury to One is An Injury to All." We oppose all forms of discrimination on the job and in our unions based on sex, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, race, national or ethnic origin, age, disability, religion or political views.
